items.title: Aguirre: “Uno se juega el turrón cada semana”
items.description: A Javier Aguirre le esperan semanas importantes al frente del Valencia, con varios enfrentamientos ante rivales directos en la lucha por la permanencia. El técnico mexicano es consciente de que cada partido tiene su peso en una temporada en la que el equipo necesita sumar cuanto antes para salir de la zona de descenso, aunque recordó que la exigencia forma parte de su trabajo diario. “Me cuesta mucho hablar de mí mismo, del pasado y del futuro, uno se juega el turrón y el cargo cada semana. Estamos expuestos a la crítica, al análisis público y el que no entienda esto no sirve para el cargo. No sé la Liga que me juego, pero sé que es muy importante el partido de mañana”, afirmó en la previa del duelo ante el Rayo Vallecano.

items.title: Ousmane Dembélé
items.description: Ousmane Dembélé est un footballeur international français né à Vernon en 1997. Jeune surdoué formé en Normandie et au stade rennais, il explose à Dortmund avant de rejoindre le FC Barcelone pour pallier le départ de Neymar au PSG, c'est à l'époque le deuxième plus gros transfert de l'histoire du football. L'adaptation, gênée par les blessure, n'est pas simple pour l'ailier français, qui parvient tout de même à se faire une place en équipe de France dans le groupe qui devient champion du monde en 2018. Absent en 2020, il est de nouveau de la partie en 2022 et fait partie du 11 titulaire.

items.title: Luis Enrique entraîneur du PSG
items.description: Luis Enrique Martínez García, dit Luis Enrique, est un ancien footballeur international espagnol reconverti en entraîneur, né le 8 mai 1970 à Gijón. Ex-sélectionneur de l'équipe d'Espagne, il entraîne actuellement le Paris Saint-Germain. Il fait partie des rares joueurs à avoir joué à la fois pour le Real Madrid et pour le FC Barcelone, qu'il a également entraîné pendant trois saisons et avec qui il a remporté la Ligue des champions 2015.

items.title: "Astiazarán y Folgado no van a poder estar y de Marchal y Dani Díaz sabremos mañana"
items.description: Jon Ansotegi quiere mantener la buena imagen ofrecida por el Sanse en los últimos partidos y dar continuidad a la racha de tres jornadas sin perder. "Tuvimos una mala racha, ahora llevamos tres partidos sin perder y creo que el equipo ha dado una buena imagen en ellos. Estamos con ganas de darle continuidad a la racha y obtener tres puntos. Hemos hecho una buena aproximación al partido. Tenemos todo para competir el partido y dar nuestra mejor versión", dijo el técnico realista, que analizó un poco lo que ha cambiado en el equipo de la racha mala a esta. "Han cambiado los resultados, eso lo primero. En esos 6 partidos perdidos, en alguno teníamos la sensación de no estar lejos de ganarlos pero por lo que sea se perdieron. Cuando algo no sale bien el equipo tiene que volver a lo básico, a ser difíciles para el rival, e hicimos eso. El equipo ha dado un pasito en eso, en general. Remangarnos más y ser conscientes de que habrá siempre momentos malos en los partidos, y esos sufrirlos, ser equipo y sacarlo adelante aprovechando los nuestros. El otro día hicimos muy buen primer tiempo, que lo dijo el rival también, y estás a nada de un 0-2 al descanso", añadió.

items.title: Audero se hace fijo bajo palos en Vallecas
items.description: Dani Cárdenas estaba en el banquillo cuando Augusto Batalla se lesionó ante el Alavés en Butarque. Entró con el Rayo por delante y, ya en el descuento, evitó con una parada a Mariano que el conjunto vitoriano se llevara los tres puntos (1-1). Aquella noche de agosto cambió el reparto de la portería rayista. Tres meses después, es Emil Audero quien llega a la visita del Valencia (sábado, 16.15 h) con la confianza de Beñat San José.

items.title: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season
items.description: Past years suggest it is tough to make big positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegatedThe Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged.Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing. items.title: El Andorra se agarra a Encamp para salir del pozo
items.description: El Andorra necesita convertir las buenas sensaciones en victorias antes de que la clasificación empiece a convertirse en una amenaza todavía mayor. Con un partido pendiente ante el Mallorca, los de Carles Manso afrontan este viernes la decimoquinta jornada ante el Leganés con la urgencia de poner fin a una racha de cuatro encuentros sin ganar. Penúltimos con once puntos, los tricolores tienen la salvación a solo dos, pero necesitan recuperar la fortaleza en un Nou Estadi de la FAF donde únicamente han conseguido seis de los dieciocho puntos disputados. Su última alegría en Encamp llegó hace algo más de un mes, frente al Castellón, en uno de los triunfos de mayor mérito de la temporada. Ahora, después de un mes especialmente complicado dentro y fuera del terreno de juego, el conjunto del Principado busca un resultado que le permita respirar y, al menos provisionalmente, abandonar los puestos de descenso.

items.title: Matarazzo, un entrenador de récord que ha convertido a la Real Sociedad en un rodillo
items.description: Pellegrino Matarazzo ha caído de pie en Donostia. Lo que en un principio era  una apuesta arriesgada para relevar una etapa histórica en el banquillo de Anoeta -con el paso entre medias de Sergio Francisco- se ha transformado en una comunión perfecta entre técnico, vestuario y grada. Después de tocar el cielo la pasada campaña levantando el título de la Copa del Rey en Sevilla y devolver por la puerta grande a la Real Sociedad a la Europa League, el entrenador nacido en Nueva Jersey ha arrancado este nuevo ejercicio confirmando que aquel éxito no fue fruto de la casualidad.

items.title: Courtois y Bellingham, los próximos en renovar
items.description: El Real Madrid ha anunciado con solo 24 horas de diferencia la renovación de los contratos de Arda Güler y de Aurélien Tchouaméni, ambas hasta 2032. El club blanco se asegura así la continuidad de dos piezas clave para José Mourinho y zanja dos carpetas pendientes por más que la renovación del centrocampista francés se sellara el pasado verano, en medio del interés del Manchester United por hacerse con su fichaje.

items.title: Manchester United, a sufrir y correr
items.description: Cuando al capitán de EEUU, Tyler Adams, le instaron a destacar una cualidad de Mauricio Pochettino, en su adiós de la selección americana, citó dos: el buen ambiente y la altísima dureza en los entrenamientos. “Tuvimos días y entrenamientos muy exigentes”, confesó, alabando a la vez el trato recibido, la unidad del grupo y el compromiso colectivo logrado en la etapa con el técnico de Santa Fe. Justamente, ese es el pilar tradicional de los equipos de Pochettino: una dura preparación física para soportar un alto ritmo en los partidos, para ser dominante en ellos. Lo ha sido con EEUU, pero lo fue antes en el Southampton, en el PSG, también en el Tottenham finalista europeo del 2019 e igualmente en su breve estancia en el Chelsea. Y lo será también en el Manchester United, con el objetivo de sacar a los ‘red devils’ de su larga crisis deportiva.

items.title: Tranquilidad para Raphinha
items.description: Raphinha volvió ayer a la disciplina del FC Barcelona tras vivir una ventana de selecciones convulsa. El nuevo capitán de Brasil, que ya lo es del Barça por decisión de Flick, mostró su cara más vulnerable en una rueda de prensa antes de un partido con su equipo nacional. En su país le estaban criticando con dureza porque tras renovar con el Barcelona cometió el 'pecado' de ser sincero y explicar que había hablado con Ancelotti para que le dosificase en los dos amistosos que venían con la ‘canarinha’. Porque lo que juegan las selecciones sudamericanas mientras en Europa se disputa la Nations League, torneo menor pero oficial, son ‘bolos’ cuyo afán es básicamente recaudatorio. Por eso se van a las quimbambas a jugar esos partidos cobrados a lo grande. Sin ir más lejos, en las dos últimas ventanas de selecciones, Brasil ha ido a Australia, India y Singapur.

items.title: Hasta Luis Enrique cambió
items.description: En el fantástico documental ‘Tocats per Lucho’ apareció una explicación increíble de Luis Enrique para describir el partido más importante de su etapa como entrenador del Barça B. Se jugaba el ascenso a Segunda División frente al Sant Andreu y dejó esta perla: “Me comí todos los fundamentos del fútbol y los tiré. Puse a 18 centrales y el balón no botó ni una vez en nuestro campo. Nos merecíamos subir”.

items.title: Si Bastoni era lento en verano tampoco será Bolt en enero
items.description: Deco, en Catalunya Ràdio, dejó un titular: “Las lesiones nos obligan a valorar si traer un central”. Ciertamente, el infortunio de Christensen, Eric y Koundé dejó a Flick muy justo de efectivos atrás. Hasta el punto de que tres centrocampistas como De Jong, Espart o Fariñas han tenido que actuar como defensas. En verano, la planificación deportiva pasaba por retener a Araujo, por prescindir de Christensen y por fichar a un central. El primero de la lista de Deco no era otro que el capitán del Inter, Alessandro Bastoni.

items.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
items.description: Bruno Guimarães to feel the heat on Tyneside, Alex Scott’s return further cheers Cherries and Manchester City face favourite whipping boysAfter three Premier League defeats on the spin, Manchester City need something or someone to come along and put some pep in their step, and Fulham look like just the thing – after all, in the past 15 years these teams have played 20 times in all competitions, and City have won precisely 20 of those games. Their current run of 17 successive league wins against Fulham is the longest run of victories by one club against a single opponent in English top-flight history. It is a reflection of the changing realities of English football, and the gulf that has opened between the teams that dominate it and those who seek to challenge them, that of the top 10 such runs all but one occurred in whole or in part after 2010 and six of them have been achieved by Sheikh Mansour’s Manchester City, with Chelsea responsible for another two, Manchester United one, and Portsmouth’s postwar, 13-game supremacy over Everton – a wild ride that included two 5-0s, a 5-1, a 6-3 and a 7-0 – the anomaly. items.title: Summer signings join Lionel Messi among MLS’s top earners: Takeaways from the league’s salary release
items.description: How much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season? The latest batch of salaries lends some insightLionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Second-year LAFC forward Son Heung-min sits fourth on $11.2m.Casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami announced his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. The MLS Players’ Association lists Casimiro on a base salary of $896,004. Continue reading...

items.title: Football Daily | Football’s political gamers face off at Fifa with the real-life final boss
items.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!Although the millions of gamers who are pulling sickies would beg to differ, the release of Grand Theft Auto VI wasn’t the most exciting midnight launch involving a sprawling enterprise full of shady characters. Over in Zurich, the clock also struck 12 on the candidate deadline for next year’s Fifa presidential election, leaving those of us who have no interest in video games with our own chaotic, multi-billion-dollar sandbox where untouchable bosses bend the rules to suit themselves. While online carjackers are busy exploring a “most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world”, football’s real-life power brokers are gearing up for a March showdown in the actual city of Rabat.When I first saw the photo in yesterday’s Football Daily, I thought Mauricio Pochettino had opted for a short back and sides, presumably to pre-empt him tearing his luscious locks out in frustration at forthcoming poor results/terrible January transfer window/petulant sniping from sulky squad members. Then I realised he was in the back seat, all but entirely obscured by the rear-view mirror, in which he could perhaps see his sense of job satisfaction disappearing …” – Phil Taverner.That photo of Pochettino being chauffeured by a beefy driver answered one of my burning questions: what’s Ange Postecoglou doing these days?” – Mike Wilner (and others).This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. items.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
items.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quicklyIt’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it.But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio. From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

items.title: Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’
items.description: A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt. Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficultyIn December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close.Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. Rebel forces had swept out of the northwest, taking Aleppo and were pushing south towards the capital, 350km away, threatening to topple the now-former president, Bashar al-Assad. Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home. items.title: La Asociación Cultural El Caño de Vezdemarbán recauda 737 euros para la lucha contra el cáncer
items.description: La Asociación Cultural «El Caño de Vezdemarbán», entidad sin ánimo de lucro fundada en 2008 en la localidad zamorana de Vezdemarbán, y cuya labor se centra en impulsar la vida cultural, festiva y solidaria del municipio, ha hecho entrega de un donativo de 737 euros a la Asociación Española Contra el Cáncer (AECC) en su sede de Toro. La cantidad ha sido recaudada gracias a la marcha solidaria celebrada el pasado 31 de octubre en la localidad. La iniciativa reunió alrededor de un centenar de vecinos que participaron en un recorrido de dos kilómetros, pensado para que pudieran sumarse personas de todas las edades, desde los más pequeños hasta los mayores. Una vez finalizada la marcha, los asistentes compartieron un chocolate con churros en un ambiente de convivencia y solidaridad.

items.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
items.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation“Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes.The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group.As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it. Continue reading...

items.title: ‘He wants to change lives’: the story behind Bukayo Saka’s Sócrates award
items.description: By supporting the non-profit BigShoe, the Arsenal forward has earned deserved plaudits for his social conscienceValerie Fiesser will never forget her surprise when Bukayo Saka contacted her out of the blue in 2022, asking whether he could help support a project in Nigeria. “I remember thinking: ‘Is this really Bukayo writing us an email?’” says the president of BigShoe, a non-profit organisation based in Frankfurt that has helped more than 10,000 children worldwide. “But that’s how he is. He’s always asking what more we can do.”Four years on from that unexpected email, Fiesser was given the secret task of reaching out for a letter for Saka to read from the podium when he was presented with the Sócrates award at last month’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in London for his humanitarian work. She got the words from Byiringiro, a 14-year-old from Rwanda who had his eyesight restored after having surgery thanks to a BigShoe initiative. Continue reading...

items.title: Echoes of Azteca but not like Argentina: fearless England start afresh in Madrid
items.description: ‘We will not go back on this way of playing,’ says Thomas Tuchel after he delivered response to World Cup criticsThomas Tuchel made defensive substitutions as England protected a lead. He finished with three centre-backs on the pitch. His team could not get out of their half in the final part of the game. So close your eyes and imagine an alternate universe in which James Trafford did not make his stunning double save in stoppage time on Sunday and England had drawn 3-3 with Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium rather than won 3-2. The reaction would not have been kind because Tuchel has been here before.The head coach wanted to push one particular comparison from the World Cup over the summer. “It was Mexico reloaded,” he said, with a nod towards the 3-2 last-16 win at the Azteca Stadium and it fitted like a glove – down to the detail of Jarell Quansah and red cards. items.title: Spain in pain as historic run ends but De la Fuente feels best is yet to come
items.description: While the head coach, players and Spanish press were magnanimous in defeat, there was pride mixed in with disappointment – and confidence the future is still bright“With every game, defeat gets closer,” Luis de la Fuente had said and on Sunday night it finally came. Spain had lost only one competitive game since Scotland in March 2023 back when the coach hadn’t won anything and didn’t look like he ever would – and that solitary loss was on penalties in the 2025 Nations League final. Statistically, they said, penalties don’t count, so while Portugal lifted the trophy that night, the team that won the European Championship and World Cup in the summers either side also claimed a Fifa record of 44 official games unbeaten. And then England turned up at the Metropolitano.A night that started with Iker Casillas, Fernando Torres and Fernando Llorente handing the World Cup to Unai Simón ended with Spain trying to overhaul a shock 3-0 deficit. Against 10 men and led by a superb Lamine Yamal, Spain made De la Fuente think for a while that they would too, but it wasn’t to be. Continue reading...

items.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
items.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managersSign up for our free newsletter hereWho should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom SAlthough the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling.This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. items.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
items.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreakLast week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result.Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. Continue reading...

items.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
items.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL drawSonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. items.title: Which football club has had most international captains in the same team? | The Knowledge
items.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managersMail us with all of your questions and answers“Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?”A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. Continue reading...

items.title: Ultimate 1-50: the male footballers best associated with each squad number
items.description: Who is football’s most legendary No 9? Has there ever been a legendary No 28? And why exactly does Mario Balotelli love wearing No 45 so much? Here’s our list and the stories behind itThe relationship between players and numbers is a long-established one filled with memories and fascinating as well as fun stories behind them. With that in mind, the Guardian has had a go at deciding which male player is best associated with each squad number, from 1-50. Various factors were taken into consideration, including how long a player wore/has worn that number, what they achieved/have achieved in it, why they decided to wear it in the first place and, in some cases, how distinctly it has become associated with them in death. The below list is highly subjective and ultimately a bit of fun, but don’t let that stop you being shocked and furious in equal measure.*** Continue reading...
